source.title: Frivolous Units: Wider Networks Are Not Really That Wide
source.authors: Stephen Casper; X. Boix; Vanessa D'Amario; Ling Guo; Martin Schrimpf; Kasper Vinken; Gabriel Kreiman

record.tranche_reason: The study sweeps network width and measures test or validation accuracy, but does not locate an interpolation threshold or apply the original double-descent analysis.
record.gate_note: Figure 1 reports width-sweep accuracy results relevant to the size-versus-test-performance part of V1. The paper does not measure whether models just fit the training set at any particular width. Double-descent findings cited from other work are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The paper takes 'accuracy does not degrade with width' as its premise and studies prunable and redundant units. Figure 1's width sweeps (1/4x–4x) are motivating context, not a double-descent test. They do not locate or span the interpolation threshold. Most models are already heavily overparameterized and trained with regularization or early stopping, which are known to hide the peak. So the absence of a peak cannot bear on V1. Random-label test accuracy is uninformative.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that wider networks keep or improve accuracy while developing disproportionately more prunable and/or redundant units, which act as unit-level complexity constraints (implicit regularization). Such units also appear under random labels, so they imply implicit regularization but not generalization. Double descent is only cited in related work.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies width and measures accuracy alongside prunability and redundancy; it does not sweep around an identified interpolation threshold or measure a double-descent curve.
record.method_sensitivity: Accuracy is examined across architectures, datasets, label conditions, and initialization choices; the paper also reports supplemental accuracy sweeps under different training settings.

fits_no_version.finding: In regularized or early-stopped ImageNet and CIFAR-10 networks widened from 1/4x to 4x, test accuracy stays flat or improves. The share of prunable and redundant units grows faster than width (gain g>2 in most cases).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Past heavy overparameterization, wider networks do not lose test accuracy; unit-level redundancy and prunability grow superlinearly with width.

record.problems: The width sweeps do not identify the interpolation threshold or show whether the tested ranges span it. Figure 1 accuracy values are presented graphically, without exact values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Supplemental accuracy plots in Figures E6–E11 and the late-training accuracy plot in Figure E12 are not separately extracted. The paper presents these as initialization or training-setting checks for its frivolous-unit analyses, and they do not locate an interpolation threshold or report a double-descent curve.

untested.parts: Location of the interpolation threshold; whether test error peaks near it; any sweep spanning under- to over-parameterized widths without early stopping or regularization.
All; no test error over training epochs (Fig. E12 covers only post-convergence epochs, for unit analyses).
All; sample size is not varied.
All; random labels are used, but partial label noise is not swept against test error.
All; the 'effective complexity' framing is about frivolous units, not a reparameterization of the risk curve.

record.verdict_notes: I reject the record's 'challenges' label for V1. The sweeps never locate or span the interpolation threshold. The models use regularization, data augmentation or early stopping, known to mask the peak. Random-label runs give chance-level test accuracy. A flat or rising curve in this regime is consistent with the post-threshold second descent, so it neither supports nor challenges V1. Accuracy values are figure-only.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not locate the size at which the training set is just fit, establish whether a peak occurs near that size, or test the complete fall-rise-fall curve across a range spanning that point.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Varied network width and measured ImageNet validation top-1 accuracy.
rows.note: The text says wider networks do not degrade in test performance; the plotted values are not transcribed in the text. The interpolation threshold is not identified.
rows.check: The width range 1/4x–4x is not shown to straddle the interpolation threshold, and the model is trained with BN, data augmentation and weight decay. A monotone curve cannot show whether a peak exists near the threshold. 'Absent' overstates what the figure shows.

rows.subject: Inception-v3
rows.operation_detail: Varied network width and measured ImageNet validation top-1 accuracy.
rows.note: The text says wider networks do not degrade in test performance. No 2x or 4x full Inception-v3 models were trained.
rows.check: Same as r1. Only 1/4x–1x was trained, with regularization, and no interpolation threshold is identified.

rows.subject: Inception-v3-layer
rows.operation_detail: Varied one layer's width and measured ImageNet validation top-1 accuracy.
rows.note: The text says wider networks do not degrade in test performance; only one layer's width was varied.
rows.check: Only a single layer's width is varied, so total model size barely changes. This does not trace model-wise capacity across the threshold.

rows.subject: AlexNet
rows.operation_detail: Varied network width and measured CIFAR-10 test accuracy.
rows.note: The figure describes regularized AlexNets. The text states that increasing model size resulted in equal or improved performance.
rows.check: Trained with early stopping on a validation set, and regularized (per the Fig. 1b caption). Early stopping suppresses model-wise peaks, and no threshold is located.

rows.subject: AlexNet-Random
rows.operation_detail: Varied network width and measured CIFAR-10 test accuracy.
rows.note: The text states that models of 1x size or greater fit the random-label training set with at least 99% accuracy; it does not give exact test accuracies.
rows.check: Trained on fully random labels, so test accuracy against true labels is at chance at every width. The measure cannot show a double-descent shape. The ≥99% train fit at 1x+ is a training-fit check, not a test-error value.

rows.subject: ResNet56
rows.operation_detail: Varied network width and measured CIFAR-10 test accuracy.
rows.note: The text states that increasing model size resulted in equal or improved performance.
rows.check: Regularized (BN, data augmentation, weight decay), and the sweep is not shown to span the threshold.

rows.subject: ResNet56-Random

rows.check: Random labels make test accuracy chance-level, so the measure cannot show the effect.

reader_labels.reason: The paper reports no degradation in test performance as width increases, rather than a reported rise in error; rows r1–r10. The study does not establish whether these sweeps span the interpolation threshold.
